name: G9 T3 W05 - Hoaxes and Fakes - 9A and 9B
description: Check online claims using sources and evidence. Review 10 words. Complete Flashcards, Matching and Fill in Blank once each this week. Ungraded formative practice.

words.definition: False or inaccurate information, whether or not the person sharing it intends to mislead.
words.example: A person may spread misinformation while believing it is true.

words.definition: False information deliberately shared to mislead people.
words.example: Inventing a false story to fool readers is disinformation.

words.definition: Checking an online source by leaving its page and consulting other sources.
words.example: I use lateral reading to investigate who runs an unfamiliar website.

words.definition: Support for a claim from additional independent evidence.
words.example: Corroboration from an independent source makes the claim better supported.

words.definition: A statement that can be examined using evidence.
words.example: The claim says that the video shows a real rescue.

words.definition: Information that helps show whether a claim is supported.
words.example: The original recording provides evidence about how the video was made.

words.definition: The person, organization or original material that provides information.
words.example: I check the source before repeating a surprising story.

words.definition: How trustworthy a person or source is for a particular question.
words.example: Relevant expertise and accurate reporting can support credibility.

words.definition: The surrounding details that help explain information.
words.example: The date and location give context to an old photograph.

words.definition: A deliberate trick meant to make people believe something false.
words.example: The invented rescue was a hoax designed to fool viewers.
